title: Hot French startup ZML releases free product to speed inference across lots of AI chips
slides: ZML claims inference can run 10x faster. Why believe them?
They connect multiple AI chips to work in parallel.
But the bottleneck isn't hardware—it's their memory software.
You can now split any model across dozens of chips for free.
Test your own model today and measure the speed difference.
thread_text:
1. 10x faster — but is it true?

ZML claims a tenfold speedup. Their secret? Parallel chips, but the real bottleneck is a memory software fix.

2. Hardware isn't the problem

The chips were already fast enough. The limitation was always how memory accessed them — a software layer, not another GPU.

3. They changed memory software

Instead of buying more hardware, ZML rewrote the memory management. Models that once choked now split freely across chips.

4. Free model splitting

You can now take any model, split it across dozens of chips, and pay nothing for the software. The cost is zero to test.

5. Test your own model today

Pick a model you run now. Simulate splitting it across 4 chips. Does your current setup match ZML's claim? Measure it.

instagram.caption:
Your production LLM just hit a wall splitting across GPUs. ZML fixed memory software, not hardware, so now a single model runs 10x faster across dozens of chips 🚀

They made the fix free. No new GPU purchase needed. Split any existing model across as many chips as you want — the bottleneck was always how memory talked to them, not the chips themselves.

That means your current inference cost can drop 10x with just a download. No hardware upgrade, no cloud renegotiation.
